speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of ulcerative colitis, inconsistent condom use, and abnormal liver function tests, I need to rule out Hepatitis B or C. Have you ever tested positive for Hepatitis B or C in the past, or do you have any other known sexually transmitted infections?

REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_Serology (HBsAg, Anti-HCV)
REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel (ALT, AST, Alk Phos, Total Bilirubin)

speaker: Doctor
text: The liver function tests show a significant elevation in Alkaline Phosphatase (460 U/L) with only mild elevation in transaminases, suggesting an obstructive or infiltrative process rather than typical viral hepatitis. Given your history of Ulcerative Colitis, have you been diagnosed with Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC), and do you notice any visible changes in your stool color, such as it becoming pale or clay-colored? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) with secondary biliary cirrhosis.

The clinical picture of fatigue, severe pruritus, scleral icterus, and significantly elevated Alkaline Phosphatase in a patient with Ulcerative Colitis is classic for PSC. The negative Hepatitis serology rules out viral hepatitis, and the high Alk Phos confirms a cholestatic process. I have already requested an Abdominal Ultrasound to visualize the biliary tree for the characteristic "beaded" appearance; please await those results to confirm the diagnosis.
